transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... ever since my grandson was killed, things just haven't been right. My daughter, she'll come over and sit right beside me, just holding my hand. And I know I love her, I know that in my head, but... I just cannot feel the warmth of it inside me at all anymore.
Since your grandson passed away, have you found yourself losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or have you been feeling like life isn't worth living?

No, I... I wouldn't say that. I don't feel like life isn't worth living. It's just... I'm just so numb to everything right now. I haven't really been doing much of anything since it happened, to be honest. I just sit there. I don't think about doing the things I used to enjoy, I just... I don't feel much of anything at all.
Do you find yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more often since your grandson passed away?
No, I... I don't think so. I know it wasn't my fault, so I don't really blame myself for what happened to him. I don't feel guilty. It's really just... just that emptiness I mentioned.
Since your grandson passed away, have you noticed a decrease in your ability to feel pleasure or joy, even during moments that used to make you happy?

Yes, that's... that's really what I was trying to say when we first started talking. Like with my daughter holding my hand. That used to bring me such comfort and joy. I know I love her, but I just can't feel any of that warmth or happiness inside me anymore. I just can't seem to feel the good things at all.
Is it only during moments related to your grandson’s loss that you feel numb, or do you also feel this way even during other parts of your day that aren’t connected to his passing?

I think it's just... it's all the time. I haven't really noticed a difference, to be honest. It doesn't seem to matter if I'm thinking about him or just... sitting in the living room trying to pass the time. It's just a constant feeling, no matter what part of the day it is or what's going on around me.
Have you noticed that your emotional response to things in general has become more limited or restricted since your grandson passed away?

I'm not entirely sure what you mean by restricted. I... I haven't really noticed anything besides what I just told you. It's just that same empty feeling. I don't think I have any other kind of reaction to things right now, just... just that numbness I mentioned.
Have you noticed that you don't react emotionally to things that used to make you smile, laugh, or feel good, even things that aren't related to your grandson?

Well, like I was saying, it's just that same empty feeling all the time. I don't really smile or laugh at anything anymore. Even if my favorite show is on or... or something nice happens, I just don't feel anything about it. It's just all blank now.
Even in moments that used to bring you happiness or love, do you find that you can't feel those emotions at all now, like they're just gone?

Yes, they really are just... gone. That's actually why I came in to see someone. Since my grandson was killed... my daughter can sit right beside me, holding my hand, and I know I love her. I know it. But I just cannot feel the warmth of it inside me at all anymore.
Even in moments that used to bring you happiness or love, do you find that you can't feel those emotions at all now, like they're just gone?

Like I just said, yes, those good feelings are completely gone. I don't feel the happiness or the love at all anymore. 

What happens instead is... well, I'll just be going about my day, trying to do something normal like folding a quilt square or reaching for my tea, and all of a sudden I hear those shots again. I see him lying there outside the community center. It is exactly like it's happening right in front of me all over again.
Do you often find yourself experiencing those flashbacks or feeling like the shooting is happening all over again, even when you're not thinking about it?

Yes, that's exactly it. Like I was just saying, I don't even have to be thinking about him or what happened. I'll just be sitting there folding a quilt square, or reaching for my tea, and out of nowhere... I hear those shots again. I see him lying there outside the community center. It just feels exactly like it is happening right in front of me all over again.
Do you find yourself feeling sad, hopeless, or emotionally empty most of the time, not just during reminders of your grandson’s death?

I wouldn't say I feel sad or hopeless most of the time... it's really just the emptiness. Like I said before, I just don't feel much of anything at all. It's not a deep sadness, it's more like... a blankness. I'm just empty.
Since your grandson passed away, have you noticed that you no longer take pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, even those that had nothing to do with him?

Well, I suppose... I mean, I don't really do much of anything anymore. I used to quilt with the ladies at the church, and I liked tending to my African violets. But now... I just don't have the interest. It's not that I try to do them and don't enjoy it, I just don't even try. Like I said, it's just that blankness. I don't care about the quilting or the plants or anything else.

Since your grandson passed away, have you found yourself withdrawing from people or activities that used to be important to you, even those that reminded you of him or brought you comfort in the past?

Yes, I have. I've stopped going to my walking club entirely. And... I just cannot bring myself to help with the funeral repast planning. It's hard to admit, because those are the very people and duties my family really depends on me for right now. But I just can't do it. I've pulled away from all of it.
Since your grandson passed away, have you been experiencing persistent feelings of fear, anger, or intense sadness connected to what happened to him?
No, not really. Like I was saying before, it's not anger or deep sadness. I'm not scared, either. It's just that... blank feeling. I just feel empty.
